Veilant offers a solid work-life balance and flexible remote work options. At Veilant, you’ll work with the most talented software developers, systems engineers, and subject matter experts, building tools and systems that make a real difference. You should be comfortable at the Linux command line, understand how networks actually work, and be able to move across operating systems, virtualization, cloud, security, automation, and documentation without needing everything perfectly defined up front. The right person has strong technical curiosity, a bias for action, and enough hands-on experience to know when to move fast and when to slow down and do it right. The work is hands-on, technical, and important. You will help engineer, deploy, secure, and maintain mission-focused infrastructure in a collaborative environment with other mid-to-senior engineers. You will not be on an island. You will be supported by a highly technical 24x7 Network and Security Operations Center that keeps eyes on the environment around the clock. That means you can focus on engineering, improvement, and problem solving without living under constant on-call pressure or rolling out updates at 0-dark-30. You will also get your choice of laptop: MacBook, Windows, or Linux. Windows is technically an option, but seriously, why? Mac or Linux is obviously the correct answer. We also try to make the environment human. We have an active board game group, Xbox gamers, and people who genuinely enjoy hanging out with other geeks. If you want to work with serious technical people, solve real problems, and still have a life outside of work, this is a good place to do that. What You Should Be Good At You should be the kind of engineer who can look at a problem holistically and start breaking it down. Maybe it is DNS. Maybe it is routing. Maybe it is Linux permissions. Maybe it is a firewall rule. Maybe it is VMware. Maybe it is AWS. Maybe it is something weird that only shows up once every few weeks. You do not need to know everything, but you do need to know how to troubleshoot, learn, ask good questions, and keep moving. We Care About People Who Can Build reliable systems Understand how packets move Troubleshoot across layers Automate the boring stuff Write things down clearly Improve the environment, not just maintain it Work independently without going dark Collaborate well with other technical engineers Communicate clearly when something is broken, blocked, or at risk What You Will Accomplish In The First Six Months Within your first six months, you should be able to: Deploy hardened Linux systems and bring them into production Take ownership of assigned systems and understand how they fit into the larger environment Support infrastructure across on-prem, virtualized, and cloud environments Identify areas where infrastructure can be improved, simplified, or better secured Partner with DevOps to automate manual or repetitive tasks Improve monitoring, alerting, and operational visibility Produce documentation that helps the next engineer troubleshoot faster Technologies in Our Stack You do not need to be an expert in every one of these, but you should be comfortable working across a real infrastructure stack. Debian and Ubuntu Linux Windows Server in limited areas VMware ESXi, vSphere, vCenter, and vSAN AWS, GCP, and related cloud services Docker and related container technologies Ansible and Jenkins Cisco IOS, Cisco NX-OS, Juniper, and Fortinet/FortiGate IPSec, WireGuard, OpenVPN, MACsec, and TLS OSPF, VRF, and MPLS Monitoring, logging, and operational visibility tools Qualifications Must Haves Active Top Secret clearance 8+ years of relevant hands-on systems, infrastructure, cloud, or network engineering experience Strong Linux experience, including real command-line troubleshooting and administration Solid understanding of TCP/IP, the OSI model, and networking fundamentals Experience troubleshooting across systems, networks, virtualization, cloud, and security boundaries Familiarity with secure tunneling and encryption technologies such as IPSec, OpenVPN, WireGuard, TLS, or MACsec Ability to work with other mid-to-senior engineers in a technical, collaborative environment Strong technical aptitude and curiosity Bias for action Ability to work independently and follow through Clear written and verbal communication skills Nice to Haves Experience with AWS, GCP, or hybrid cloud environments Experience with Ansible, Jenkins, or similar automation tools Experience with Docker or Kubernetes Experience with VMware vSAN and larger vSphere environments Experience with Cisco NX-OS, Juniper, or FortiGate platforms Understanding of OSPF, VRF, MPLS, MACsec, and related network/security concepts Experience working in secure, classified, or mission-focused environments Ability to create diagrams and documentation that engineers want to use Who This Role Is For This role is for someone who enjoys infrastructure. You like Linux. You like understanding how systems fit together. You like solving problems that are not clean or obvious. You probably have opinions about good documentation, bad firewall rules, broken monitoring, cloud sprawl, and why “just reboot it” is not a strategy. We are looking for someone who wants ownership, not just tasks. If you want to help build and operate reliable infrastructure in a serious environment, this is the kind of role where you can make an immediate impact. Collaborative Culture: Be part of a team that supports each other and works toward shared goals. Career Growth: Opportunities for professional development and career advancement.
